newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana c.bank says reckless to delink pula/rand.
newsitem.headline: Botswana c.bank says reckless to delink pula/rand.

text.p: The temptation to create a strong pula would be a reckless approach to managing the nation's finances, the Bank of Botswana said in its annual economic review for 1996.
The Bank has been repeatedly criticised for indirectly linking the pula to the South African rand, which has depreciated sharply against major currencies since February 1996.
Critics have said this might protect a fledgling non-mineral export industry, but deters investors, who are wary of falling currencies.
Diamond exports, traded in dollars, accounted for 33 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), 66 percent of export earnings and 48 percent of government revenues.
More than 80 percent of non-mineral exports were destined for South Africa and traded in rands. The same percentage of imports also came from South Africa.

The Bank said exchange rate policy operated in line with the national objectives of sustained development and diversification of production and to create significant employment for the 20-25 percent of working age Batswana who were unemployed.
Over the last 21 years, since the pula was introduced, its real exchange rate against the rand has never fluctuated by more than 10 per cent from its nominal value.

The Bank also added it expected Botswana's foreign reserves to have doubled by the end of National Development Plan 8 (NDP8) in 2002. "The reserves are projected to total some 37,000 million pula," the review says.
